headline: CBA's cash NPAT increased $730 million or 7.1% to $10,982 million in FY26 (ev-70). Total operating income grew 6.2% to $30,224 million, driven by a $1,563 million increase in Net Interest Income (NII) (ev-59). Operating performance rose 6.5% to $16,469 million, supported by underlying operating expense growth of 5.6% to $13,585 million and notable items of $170 million (ev-68, ev-73). Loan impairment expense increased $62 million to $788 million (ev-21), while corporate tax expense rose $208 million to $4,699 million (ev-33). Statutory NPAT was $10,866 million (ev-37).

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563 million or 7% to $25,586 million (ev-59). The bank attributes this to an $92 billion or 8% increase in average interest earning assets (AIEA), partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in net interest margin (NIM) to 2.05% (ev-60). AIEA growth was driven by increases in home loans ($32 billion), business/corporate loans ($27 billion), non-lending assets ($17 billion), and liquid assets ($15 billion) (ev-61 to ev-65). NIM excluding liquids was stable (ev-66).

Other operating income increased $196 million or 4% to $4,638 million (ev-1). Commissions rose $135 million to $2,234 million (ev-2), lending fees increased $12 million to $924 million (ev-3), funds management income grew $12 million to $134 million (ev-5), other income increased $46 million to $156 million (ev-6), and trading income decreased $9 million to $1,190 million (ev-4).

Underlying operating expenses increased $719 million or 6% to $13,585 million (ev-16). Staff expenses rose $288 million to $8,258 million (ev-12), occupancy and equipment expenses decreased $19 million to $938 million (ev-13), IT services expenses increased $393 million to $2,782 million (ev-14), and other expenses rose $57 million to $1,607 million (ev-15). The cost-to-income ratio improved 30 basis points to 44.9% (ev-19).
Restructuring and notable items increased $40 million to $170 million (ev-17). This represents a higher expense drag compared to the prior year's $130 million.

Loan impairment expense increased $62 million or 9% to $788 million (ev-21). The increase was driven by Retail Banking Services (+$106 million to $378 million) (ev-22) and New Zealand (+$11 million to $66 million) (ev-23), partially offset by Business Banking (-$45 million to $310 million) (ev-24) and Institutional Banking and Markets (-$16 million to $33 million) (ev-25). The loss rate increased 1 basis point to 8 bps (ev-26).

Corporate tax expense increased $208 million or 5% to $4,699 million (ev-33). The effective tax rate decreased 50 basis points to 30.0%, primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses (ev-34).

notable_items: Restructuring and notable items: $170 million in FY26 vs $130 million in FY25 (ev-17).
limitations: Capped at 80: operating_expenses -719 $m, notable_items -40 $m. The records these claims cite do not state those numbers, so each one is arithmetic over the evidence rather than a figure read from it.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.
